newsitem.title: INDIA: India cyclone death toll climbs to 224.
newsitem.headline: India cyclone death toll climbs to 224.

text.p: The death toll from a cyclone that struck India's eastern state of Andhra Pradesh has climbed to 224, relief workers said on Thursday.
"The death toll has gone to 224, and it may climb further," H.S. Brahma, the top state official coordinating relief operations, told Reuters.

Communications were disrupted after the cyclone wreaked havoc in the rich rice-growing districts of East and West Godavari, officials said. In East Godavari, where 100,000 homes were destroyed or damaged, 169 people died.
"Now the cyclone has weakened and is moving into the northern coastal areas and the internal Telangana region, where there is heavy rainfall and strong winds," Brahma said.

The storm, with winds of between 100 and 120 kmh (62 mph to 75 mph), struck on Wednesday evening, flattening homes, destroying crops and cutting transport and communication links. Officials are still unable to estimate the full extent of the damage to crops.
Last month, floods damaged 1.13 million hectares (3.1 million acres) of land, about eight per cent of the farmland in Andhra Pradesh.
